about.intro_content: Prof. Xing Zhang is a Professor and Chief Physician in the Department of Immunotherapy and Medical Oncology of Melanoma and Sarcoma at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou. She specialises in immunotherapy of solid tumours, molecular targeted drug therapy, and medical treatment of bone and soft tissue sarcoma and melanoma.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Zhang studied at Boston University Medical School (2001–2003) before completing her doctoral degree in oncology at Sun Yat-sen University in 2004. She is one of Guangdong's Outstanding Young Medical Talents and Principal Investigator of 5 National Natural Science Foundation projects. She has published dozens of SCI papers as first or corresponding author in journals including Oncogene, Molecular Cancer, British Journal of Cancer and Clinical Cancer Research, and has participated in drafting 3 national medical treatment guidelines for sarcoma.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Xing Zhang

items.question: Does Prof. Xing Zhang accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to melanoma or sarcoma at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Zhang's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Zhang specialises in immunotherapy and molecular targeted therapy for melanoma and bone/soft tissue sarcoma.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Zhang involved in clinical trials for sarcoma or melanoma?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Zhang is Principal Investigator on a phase I trial of Super1 TCR-T cell therapy for NY-ESO-1-positive advanced solid tumours, including sarcoma and melanoma.

items.question: Has Prof. Zhang contributed to national treatment standards?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Zhang has participated in drafting 3 national medical treatment guidelines for sarcoma and holds leadership roles in national and provincial sarcoma professional committees.
